t: The Lisp Philosophy: Computing's Foundational Divide
s: This article explores the foundational divide in computing between Turing's imperative, stateful machines and Church's functional, stateless lambda calculus, embodied by Lisp. It contrasts Lisp's functional approach, homoiconicity, and structural pipelines with imperative languages and Unix byte-stream pipelines, illustrating how Lisp offers an alternative 'engine' for computation.
sub: Turing's imperative/stateful vs. Church's functional/stateless computing
Tail Call Optimization (TCO) for efficient recursion
Lisp structural pipelines vs. Unix byte-stream pipelines
Lisp Macros for dynamic language extension
